section_summary: This section comprises diplomatic records of the American Embassy in Tokyo from July through September 1939, including the conclusion of Monthly Report No. 153 (June), the full Monthly Report No. 154 (July), a Department of State instruction commending the July report, and the transmittal and opening pages of Monthly Report No. 155 (August). Major topics include escalating Japanese-American tension following the U.S. notification of termination of the 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation, repeated American protests over Japanese air bombings of Chungking and mission properties, and assaults on American nationals in China. It also documents the Anglo-Japanese negotiations in Tokyo concerning the Tientsin Concession crisis and the Craigie-Arita formula, severe Soviet-Japanese border hostilities along the Halha River (Nomonhan), and Japan's intensifying domestic economic and labor mobilization controls.

subfiles.about: Concluding pages of the Embassy's monthly report on conditions in Japan for June 1939 and its formal transmittal despatch.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: This concluding section of Monthly Report No. 153 covers Japanese domestic economic controls, including criticism of commodity price ceilings, the proposed yen-bloc foreign exchange pool, creation of the Foreign Trade Commission under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, amendments to foreign exchange control laws, and the enforcement of the Law for the Protection of Military Resources Secrets. It reviews state finances including China Incident bond issues, Bank of Japan silver price reductions, petroleum sales unification, state shipping control, wholesale price indices, and foreign trade statistics. Complete schedules of despatches (Nos. 3919-4008) and telegrams (Nos. 251-308) sent by the Embassy to the Department during June 1939 are appended, followed by Chargé Eugene H. Dooman's formal transmittal despatch No. 4043.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4043, Tokyo, Enclosing Monthly Report on Conditions in Japan for June 1939 (Report No. 153)

subfiles.about: Comprehensive monthly report on political, diplomatic, and economic conditions in Japan during July 1939.
keywords: Treaty of Commerce and Navigation of 1911
subfiles.summary: Report No. 154 documents extensive diplomatic developments in July 1939, headlined by the United States Government's formal notice on July 26 of the termination of the 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation, along with emphatic American protests against indiscriminate Japanese bombings of Chungking and mission properties across China and assaults on American citizens. It provides detailed analysis of the Anglo-Japanese Tokyo conference regarding the Tientsin Concession and the Craigie-Arita formula, severe border clashes between Soviet-Mongolian and Japanese-Manchurian forces along the Halha River, disputes over North Saghalien concessions, and the conclusion of a trade agreement with Germany. On the domestic front, the report surveys the invocation of the National General Mobilization Labor Conscription Ordinance, the creation of the Asia Promotion Commission, elections in the House of Peers, fiscal tax reform plans, and monthly economic and foreign trade indicators, concluding with comprehensive lists of despatches (Nos. 4000-4054) and telegrams (Nos. 309-376) sent during July.
subfiles.title: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of July 1939 (Report No. 154)

subfiles.about: Instruction acknowledging Embassy despatch No. 4108 and commending Third Secretary James Espy for preparing the July 1939 report on conditions in Japan.
subfiles.from: G. S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary of State George S. Messersmith informs Ambassador Joseph C. Grew that the Department received and read with great interest Embassy despatch No. 4108 of August 22, 1939, enclosing the review of conditions in Japan for July 1939. The Department commends the report's clear and logical presentation, noting that it is especially helpful for reference purposes. Ambassador Grew is requested to convey to the drafting officer, Third Secretary James Espy, the Department's appreciation for the high quality of his work.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1819 to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew Commending the July 1939 Report on Conditions in Japan
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Covering despatch and initial ten pages of the Embassy's monthly report on conditions in Japan during August 1939.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 4134 transmits Report No. 155 reviewing political, diplomatic, and economic conditions in Japan for August 1939. The report details vigorous American representations concerning continued Japanese military assaults on American citizens (including Smithberger, Scannell, and Richard), anti-foreign agitation in China, blocked funds of the American President Lines, and the broader implications of the Tientsin negotiations and the 1911 commercial treaty termination. It also covers the breakdown of the Anglo-Japanese conference in Tokyo over Japanese demands concerning North China currency and the surrender of Chinese silver stocks in the British Concession, despite Britain's handover of four Chinese suspects, as well as Japanese military operations and coastal blockades in China.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4134, Tokyo, Enclosing Monthly Report on Conditions in Japan for August 1939 (Report No. 155)
